sentences.text: The genus Planicoxa was formally described by DiCroce and Carpenter in 2001, with the type species named Planicoxa venenica.
Known fossils include a well-preserved ilium, femurs, tibias, vertebrae, and other skeletal material.
While the femurs are typical for ornithopods, the ilium features a short, horizontal postacetabular process that functions as an antitrochanter.
This animal belongs to the infraorder Ornithopoda and is classified within the unranked family Iguanodontia.
Fossils were discovered in Utah, United States, within the Poison Strip Sandstone Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Grand County.
The species name venenica is Latin for "poison," referencing the Poison Strip Sandstone Member where the fossils were found.
A second species, P. depressa, was established by Carpenter and Wilson in 2008 for material originally named Camptosaurus depressus by Charles Gilmore in 1909.
The material for P. depressa was collected from the Lakota Formation near Hot Springs, South Dakota.
In 2011, P. depressa was reassigned to its own genus, Osmakasaurus.
Planicoxa venenica is estimated to have reached a length of 4.5 meters and weighed 450 kilograms.
The remains belong to at least two individuals, with an estimated length of 6 meters, a height of 2 meters, and a calculated weight of 900 kilograms.
Planicoxa lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago in the Aptian stage.
It inhabited the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 120 million years ago, in what is now North America.
